description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
In the past two years, JTC, SSR and CILC have worked together to implement the project and deliver the foreseen results. Since the start of the project, in April 2020 the implementation was affected by Covid 19. During he outbreak it was not obvious that the pandemic would be eminent for two years. We expected to deliver some trainings face to face, especially the one for spokesperson. However this has not been possible, so we suspended the activity. Despite these setbacks and obvious limitations, many trainings were converted and delivered online which ended with a significant result in the project implementation.
This chapter highlights the achievements in realising the outputs of the project as indicated in the logical framework and work plan.
_**Output 1: Strengthened Initial Training of Candidate Judges Collaboration partnership established. **_
Output 1 focussed on the upgrade and enhancement of the initial training programme for candidate judges. This output aimed to build on the previous training programme that was delivered by JTC up to March 2020. This project further aimed to support JTC to design a M&E framework including tools to assess performance of candidate judges whilst performing their duties at internship and even after appointment. Moreover, this project aimed to support JTC to develop modules, materials and improve teachers’ didactical skills. In addition, a new course on ethics and integrity was planned as part of the training package for candidate judges.
To date, the following achievements can be noted:
- **Development of M&E tools:** A working group for the development of M&E framework was established composing of 25 candidates from different institutions who were involved in the design and content of the M&E framework. This working group was formalised through a decree signed by JTC leadership. An implementation plan for the development of M&E tools was developed. Thereafter, a workshop and meetings with the working group were conducted in July 2021 from which an M&E survey for the evaluation of post candidate judges was developed and executed. - In July 2020, A 4-day **online training of trainers** and didactical skills was delivered by SSR to JTC staff. A module and lesson plan were developed for this training to be delivered by JTC once the candidate judges training starts. - **Development of module on integrity course: **A workshop with JTC leadership and Supreme Court’s Supervisory Body in Indonesia was held in January 2022 to conduct an inventory of ethical problems and how to design the course. This was necessary to tailor the training to the Indonesian context. The training has been designed by SSR but has not been delivered yet. We expect it will be delivered in the second subsequent project. - **Evaluation of PPC:** From September to November 2021 a post evaluation of the candidate judges programme (PPC) was conducted. This was done through a survey filled out by 322 graduate judges, 91 tutors and mentors, and 69 chief judges. Survey questions differed per respondent. In early November the results came in, thereafter a report with conclusion and recommendations were drawn and presented to the leadership of JTC. These results will be integrated in the training programme and approach for initial training for candidate judges. One of the recommendations was to deliver training on ethics and integrity and decision writing skills which have been incorporated already in our training programme of the project.
_**Output 2: Strengthened permanent education to improve judicial performance.**_
The second output focused on the development of training modules for the leadership and technical units of JTC, that had been derived from training needs analysis (TNA). Furthermore, this output incorporated the development and delivering of a refresher course for spokespersons. The following can be noted on progress:
- **Developed modules on TNA**: A TNA for the technical unit of JTC has been carried out in July 2020. The outcome of the TNA was a number of proposed topics for capacity building, namely: IT Skills, **decision writing skills and ethics and integrity.** JTC and SSR have worked together to deliver training on decision writing,ethics, and integrity in January and March 2022. The trainings have provided the basis and input for the modules (on decision writing, ethics and integrity?). The modules have not been completed yet as that will be done in a ToT to be carried out in July 2022 as part of the second project with JTC. The IT skills training will be delivered by the Judiciary. - **Evaluation of modules:** As the modules have not been completed and delivered, this activity has not been conducted. It will take place in the second project with JTC. - **Spokesperson training:** The refresher course for spokespersons has not been conducted as the success of this training depended much on physical presence of the candidates and trainers. This training targets spokespersons from remote areas and embraces body posture and expression as particular skills of spokesperson. This cannot be successfully transmitted online. Therefore, we chose to postpone this training until travel restrictions have been eased, unfortunately that was too late to realise under this project.
_**Output 3: Enhanced the use of e-learning and blended learning teaching methods.**_
This part of the training aimed at further enhancing the use of e-leaning and blended approach at JTC. In the past four years, JTC has transformed its training approach, it has developed modules that could be delivered through e-learning. Given the outbreak of Covid 19, the significane of e-learning has become more important especially given the geography of Indonesia. JTC was given training on e-learning so that JTC staff could further enhance skills on e-learning throughout all of it’s curricula.
Furthermore, we provided training on didactical skills online in July 2020 focusing on blended learning techniques. In March 2022, we provided training on decision writing skills also incorporating blended teaching approaches and learning through case studies. Training materials have were made and were provided to JTC.
Under output 3, the following achievements can be noted:
- Selection of topics for modules to be developed for the e-learning course has been made. - A module on didactical skills training has been developed. - Materials and case studies have been applied for decision writing training. - An inventory workshop has been conducted for module development on integrity. - Draft module on integrity is in progress.
_**Output 4: Improved management and Institutional capacity of JTC.**_
Output 4 focused on organisational development of JTC through the establishment of a management information system. Simultationously activities under output 4 supported JTC to effectively implement its multi-annual strategic plan (Renstra). In the past two years, all activities were conducted in a form of online consultation with JTC’s management team.
The following results have been achieved:
- Establishment of a working group responsible for the development of management information or MI system at JTC. - A Baseline information system of JTC which establishes the data available at JTC that is essential to develop the structure and content of the management information system. To this end, several workshops were held with the MI working group and interviews were conducted with Echelon 3 staff of JTC to gather appropriate information. - Defined management processes and developed management information ready to install in a system at JTC. The MI includes information on finance, human resources and accommodation facilities uitlised until May 2021. - Installation of MI software to gather/manage data and information for MI. - Recommendation for a change on strategic management and the decision process at JTC, provided to the JTC leadership on the installation and use of MI for strategic management. - Provisions of advise on the reorganisation of JTC units for sound management of the centre. Proposal for the optimisation of processes at JTC has been submitted to Makamah Agung (MA) for approval.

In the past year, JTC, SSR and CILC have worked intensively together to implement the project and deliver the foreseen results. Since the start of the project, in April 2020 they have been facing challenges as the result of Covid 19. For instance many staff of JTC have been ill and needed time to recover . Also, JTC and SSR needed to reorganise their trainings so that they could be offered online.
This chapter highlights progress and achievements in realising the outputs and milestones as proposed in the logical framework and work plan.
_**Output 1: Strengthened Initial Training of Candidate Judges Collaboration partnership established.**_
_Output 1 focuses on the upgrade and enhancement of the initial training programme for candidate judges. This project aims to follow up on the previous training programme that was delivered by JTC until February 2020. This project aims to support JTC to design a M&E framework including tools to assess performance of candidate judges whilst performing their duties at internship or even after appointment. Moreover, this project further supports JTC to develop modules, materials and improve teachers’ skills on didactic. In addition, a new course on ethics and integrity will be developed and delivered as part of the training package for candidate judges._
_To date, remarkable progress can be noted:_
_a) A working group for the development of M&E framework has been established composing of 25 candidates from different institutions who will be involved on the design and content of the M&E framework. This working group has been formalised through a decree signed by JTC leadership._
_b) Three meetings with the working group have convened which marked the start of the exercise. A workplan and implementation approach has been agreed upon. In addition, preparation is being undertaken for the tools and which includes questionnaire for post evaluation surveys for former candidates of the initial training._
_c) In July 2020, A 4-day online training of trainers and didactical skills was delivered by SSR to JTC staff. A module and lesson plan were developed for this training and delivered to JTC_
_d) Preparation for the ethics and integrity course are in progress._
_**Output 2: Strengthened permanent education to improve judicial performance.**_
_The second output focuses on the development of training modules for the leadership and technical units of JTC that will incorporate training needs analysis (TNA). In addition a refresher course for spokesperson will be organised in remote areas once travels are permitted. The following can be noted on progress:_
_a) A TNA for the technical unit of JTC has been carried out. The outcome of the TNA was a proposition on the topics for capacity building, namely: IT Skills, decision writing skills and ethics and integrity; This project supports JTC to develop training on decision writing and ethics and integrity. The IT skills training will be delivered by the Judiciary._
_b) The refresher course for spokespersons has not been conducted as the success of this training depends much on physical presence of the candidates and trainers._ _This training targets spokesperson from remote areas and embraces body posture and expression as particular skills of spokesperson. This cannot be easily transmitted online. Therefore, we wish to postpone this training until travel restrictions have been eased, expecting to happen in autumn 2021 or early 2022._
_c) Change of priorities of the leadership unit, has affected its engagement in the project activities. There seems little or no support needed from SSR in the training activities. So the TNA and training course for this unit have been suspended for now._
_**Output 3: Enhanced the use of e-learning and blended learning teaching methods.**_
_This part of the training aims to further enhance the use of e-leaning and blended approach at JTC. In the past four years, JTC has transformed its training approach, it has developed more than 90 modules that could be delivered through e-learning. Given the outbreak of Covid 19, e-learning has become more important. This project will support JTC to develop two new modules which can be delivered through e-learning. These are: decision writing and ethics and integrity which were chosen during the TNA in June 2020._
_So far, the following progress can be noted:_
_a) Selection of topics for modules to be developed for the e-learning course has been made._
_b) A working group for the development of the training on decision writing has been appointed._
_c) Preparation for the course on ethics and integrity are underway._
_**Output 4: Improved management and Institutional capacity of JTC.**_
_Output 4 focuses on organisational development of JTC through the establishment of a management information system and support JTC to effectively implement its multi annual strategic plan (Renstra). In the past year, all activities were conducted in a form of online consultation with JTC management team. The following results have been achieved to date:_
_a) Establishment of a working group responsible for the development of management information system at JTC;_
_b) Baseline information system of JTC which establishes the data available at JTC that is essential to develop the structure and content of the management information system. To do so, several workshop were held with the MI working group and interviews were conducted with Echelon 3 staff of JTC to gather appropriate information;_
_c) Defined management processes and developed management information ready to install in a system at JTC. The MI includes information on finance, human resources and accommodation facilities uitlised until May 2021._
_d) Recommendation for change on strategic management and decision process to be made by JTC leadership on the installation and use of MI for strategic management;_
_e) Provision of advise on reorganisation of JTC units for sound management of the centre. Proposal for reorganisation of JTC has been submitted to MA for approval._
